clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man with history of chronic kidney disease and recent heart transplantation presented with fever, chills, new holosystolic murmur, and right thigh pain. Blood cultures returned positive for Nocardia asteroides confirming nocardiosis. Imaging revealed moderate tricuspid regurgitation without initial visible vegetation and a right thigh abscess. Subsequent clinical course demonstrated a tricuspid valve vegetation by echocardiography, confirming infective endocarditis. The diagnosis was established based on microbiological, imaging, and clinical findings consistent with disseminated nocardiosis and endocarditis.
